_comment: The voices offered by the /listen doc reader. Data, not code — the picker renders this file. The FIRST entry is the default and MUST remain request-identical to what the reader sent before a picker existed: engine=auto, no voice parameter. engine=auto resolves to piper (measured on prod: piper:en_GB-alan-medium), so NEURAL is the default and stays the default.
_distinctness: Every entry differs from every other in ACCENT, ENGINE and REGISTER, not merely in speed. Measured on the production host (2 vCPU, espeak-ng 1.51, piper medium) with one fixed sentence — median f0 by autocorrelation, spectral centroid over the clip: NEURAL 98 Hz/2712 · CLASSIC 102/1994 · sAGI 113/2249 · LEADER 140/1236 · SAM 174/1860 · JAIMLA 182/2783 · ANCIENT 276/3398. Seven accents: Southern English, General American, Caribbean, Northern English, British female, Scottish, Received Pronunciation. Three neural (piper, three DIFFERENT models), four formant (espeak-ng, four DIFFERENT phoneme sets).
_trap: A voice NAME is not a voice. espeak-ng answers an unknown '+variant' with the BASE voice and no error; piper falls back to its first installed model. So a rendering cached while a variant was missing is a different voice filed under the name that was asked for — which is exactly what made this picker look broken on 2026-09-01 (LEADER/SAM/ANCIENT/JAIMLA were all one RP voice at four speeds, cached before the variants were installed at 12:23). The cache key therefore includes voice_fingerprint(): the variant file's own bytes, or the piper model's identity. Retune a variant and only its renderings expire.

voices.label: NEURAL
voices.title: neural (piper alan) — southern English, the default
voices.measured: f0 98 Hz · centroid 2712 · ~5.2x realtime on prod
voices.note: Sends engine=auto and NO voice parameter — byte-identical to the pre-picker request. engine=auto resolves through READER_ORDER to piper, so the DEFAULT IS THE NEURAL VOICE. This entry is the one that must never move.

voices.label: JAIMLA
voices.title: jaimla — neural (piper jenny), British female, unhurried
voices.measured: f0 182 Hz · centroid 2783 — the brightest voice in the set · ~6x realtime
voices.note: FEMALE, PROVEN NOT ASSERTED. Every male voice here measures below 150 Hz and every female above 180; Jaimla is the only female NEURAL voice and the only en_GB female on the host. It was en_US-lessac-medium (f0 187 but centroid 1534 — dark enough to read ambiguous through a phone speaker); jenny_dioco keeps the pitch and adds the brightness that actually carries gender, and moves her off the American accent so no two entries share one. rate 168 is barely under nominal, because softness here is unhurriedness, not slowness. The breath-and-fifth formant variant remains as en-gb-x-rp+jaimla for anyone who wants it.

voices.label: LEADER
voices.title: leaderofearth — one accent assembled from eight world Englishes (royal, US, Australian, Indian, Mexican, Brazilian, Brooklyn, Slavic); deepest and slowest voice in the set

layers.why: the reference, lower and unhurried — and the ONLY voice here

voices._eq: A BROADCAST DESK, NOT A SECOND SPEAKER. piper gives a length-scale and nothing else, so a derived voice can only be faster, slower, higher or lower — enough to be DIFFERENT, not enough to be AUTHORITATIVE, which is why the first LEADER reached for another voice to supply the character. A second voice is not character, it is company. These four bands are what a desk does to a presenter instead: +2.5 dB of chest under 170 Hz; -3.5 dB at 260-520 Hz, which is the mud that makes a low voice sound heavy rather than deep and is the single most important cut here; +4 dB across 1.9-4.2 kHz, where consonants are told apart, so the words land without the voice getting louder; and -2 dB above 5.2 kHz to keep sibilance off a voice that is now brighter in the mids. One speaker, shaped.
voices.accent: Earth — one accent assembled from royal, US, Australian, Indian, Mexican, Brazilian, Brooklyn and Slavic English, on a Caribbean base
voices.measured: f0 117.9 Hz · centroid 1484 · presence 2-5 kHz 23.7% — the deepest voice in the set, and no longer the darkest: presence was 12.4% before the retune
voices.note: A LEADER IS ONE VOICE, and it is a SHAPED one. It was the reference with an espeak overtone mixed on, and however that overtone was placed it was a second person — in the intelligibility band it formed words, and outside it it became a drone, which is worse. Two voices saying the same thing is unison, and unison is OVERLORD's idea. So: the reference at pitch 0.88 and speed 0.92 (about 88 Hz against neural's 101, a shade under a tenth slower), with a broadcast EQ instead of a companion, and the 0.85 s pause after every conclusion that makes it deliberate rather than merely slow. It inherits neural's clarity because it IS neural.

voices.label: OVERLORD
voices.title: overlord — the two saved voices in unison: neural carries the words, jaimla speaks them with him

layers.why: the reference, never stretched — it is the voice that does not move
jaimla, fitted to the reference at every phrase boundary — under him, not beside him (0.62)

voices.accent: Southern English and British female, at once
voices._from: deltaverse render/render_overlord.py (2026-09-02: "OVERLORD is two neural voices at once") — the same recipe, moved into the registry so every surface reads it instead of a copy. The earlier five-band espeak build survives as the en-earth+overlord variant and is not what this entry renders.
voices.note: UNISON HAS NO SINGLE OWNER. Two people saying the same words together is what a choir does to a solo line: the pitch stops belonging to a person and starts belonging to the statement. That is the register the realm uses about itself. The two voices do not agree on timing — same model family, same sentence, different durations, and the difference is not constant — so the second is anchored to the first at every phrase boundary rather than stretched once per block, which is exactly the failure LEADER's overtone had. Both layers are piper because two piper voices agree far more closely than piper and espeak do (measured 0.75-1.04 against 1.53-1.81).

voices._faceLabel: CLASSIC names the SLOT in the cast; H.A.L names the face speaking from it. The button shows the face, so the second and third presses are visible.

alternates.label: K.I.T.T
alternates.title: K.I.T.T — the voice of the car from the Knight Rider television show
alternates.note: hal's counterpart and deliberately its opposite everywhere hal commits. hal is warm, slow and leans on nothing; this is forward, quick and leans on quite a lot. Same en-us base so the two read as one character's two moods rather than two accents. The peak moves from 700 Hz (chest, in the room with you) to 1500 Hz (mouth, out of a dashboard).

alternates.label: T1000
alternates.title: T1000 — the Terminator 2 voice
alternates.note: The third face, and the one with no warmth in it. hal is warm and never emphasises; kitt is bright and emphasises constantly; this is neither, because it is not reassuring or helping, it is stating. Accent in voices/en-t800: w->v and th->z/d, the two features anyone can hear. Final-obstruent devoicing was deliberately NOT taken — it is characteristic and it turns 'bad' into 'bat', and a voice that cannot be trusted to say the word is not usable as a reading voice however good the impression. Measured f0 95.5 Hz against hal's 118.9 and kitt's 170.3.

alternates.label: FAIRYDUST
alternates.title: FAIRYDUST — high, soft and weightless, from the Jaimla template
alternates.note: Taken from the jaimla template and lifted an octave: same base, same interval (a perfect fifth, 3:2 — keeping the RATIO rather than the span is what makes it read as the same voice grown light rather than a different one squeaking). voicing 44 against jaimla's 62 with breath wider still, so less than half the signal is fold vibration and the rest is moving air — soft at any volume, because there is very little there to be loud with. The 4.2 kHz lift is where breath turns to sparkle. The only voice in the cast with no authority in it whatsoever, which is the point of putting it at the end of a row of machines that have nothing else.

voices.label: CLASSIC
voices.title: CLASSIC — H.A.L, the voice of HAL 9000 from 2001: A Space Odyssey
voices.note: The voice everyone misremembers as robotic. It is soft, warm and impeccably polite, and that is what makes it frightening — nothing in the delivery ever acknowledges the situation. breath is generous (he sounds at ease) while flutter and roughness are both ZERO (not one irregular moment, ever): a human voice under stress wavers and this one physically cannot. stressAmp barely moves, so no word is ever leaned on. NOTE: this entry used to be espeak-ng's untouched en-us — the honest baseline showing what formant synthesis sounds like with nothing done to it. That role is now unoccupied; say so if it is wanted back as its own entry.

voices.label: sAGI
voices.title: sAGI — neural (piper northern english male), Northern English, composed and reasoning
voices.note: NEURAL, AND NO LONGER A COPY. This was piper alan at rate 158 — the SAME MODEL as NEURAL, distinguished only by pace, which is why the picker's two neural entries sounded like one voice at two speeds. It now runs its own model: en_GB-northern_english_male-medium, 15 Hz above alan and audibly darker (centroid 2249 vs 2712), a different region of England entirely. rate 158 keeps the composed, reasoning-aloud pace that separates sAGI from LEADER's pronouncing.

voices.label: SAM
voices.title: sam — Scottish, gender neutral, appealing at rest and harsh when adamant
voices.note: Base moved from plain `en` — which is the same unmarked English CLASSIC already speaks — to en-gb-scotland, a separate phoneme set that is nobody else's here. The tuning is untouched: floor D3 146.83 Hz is the geometric mean of leaderofearth's E2 82.41 and jaimla's C4 261.63, within 2% of the f0 150 NeuralVoiceEngine gives its 'neutral' profile, and the span is a perfect fourth (4:3), the interval that resolves neither major nor minor. Harshness is loaded onto stress levels 5-7 with roughness 2: a static variant cannot detect anger, but it can choose to turn edged exactly when it insists. Stays FORMANT — no piper model on this host is gender-neutral, and shipping alan or jenny under this name would be a lie.

voices.label: ANCIENT
voices.title: ancient — Received Pronunciation, ZERO pitch range (98 98) and no pitch lift on any stress: authority from absolute
voices.accent: Received Pronunciation — zero pitch range, the absolute
voices.measured: f0 98 Hz fixed · voiced 54.8% (was 16.6%) · needs +11.5 dB make-up, down from +18.0 dB
voices.note: pitch 98 98: no range at all. A whisper with real tone under it (voiced 16.6% -> 54.8%) and no pitch lift on any stress.

voices.label: VOICEBOX
voices.title: voicebox — a 1990s speaking machine with a world accent: steady formants, no breath, over-articulated
voices.note: The sound of formant synthesis before there was compute to hide that it was formant synthesis. Sits on en-earth so the accent belongs nowhere in particular — a machine voice has no hometown, and a box built to be understood everywhere was tuned to the vowels several Englishes agree on. The giveaway is steadiness: a real vocal tract is always moving so its resonances smear, and a synthesiser holds each one exactly where it was told. breath is zero on every level, which is the single line separating a machine from a person. Measured f0 128.2 Hz; whisper round-trip WER 23.1% — the character costs some clarity and that is the character.

voices.label: ZEN
voices.title: ZEN — one English assembled from the Englishes of East Asia: syllable-timed, unhurried
voices._alternates: THE LABEL DOES NOT CHANGE, AND THAT IS THE FEATURE. Every other alternate in this file renames its button — CLASSIC becomes H.A.L, then K.I.T.T — because those are different characters and you should be able to see which one you picked. ZEN's second face is the same voice in a different body, and announcing it would tell you what to hear before you heard it. Press again; the only indicator is the sound.
voices.note: Built the way en-earth was — the features Japanese, Korean, Cantonese, Mandarin and Tibetan speakers of English AGREE on, so it imitates none of them. Syllable timing is where the calm actually lives: every one of those languages is syllable- or mora-timed where English is stress-timed, and syllables of even length do not rush. The l/r merger and any vowel substitution that changes which WORD is heard were deliberately left out, because a voice that cannot be understood is not calm, it is obscure. Measured f0 118.5 Hz.

voices.label: TRANSLATOR
voices._surfaces: DELTAVERSE ONLY. The mindX reader is a document reader and its cast is finished; these are experiments in tracking and placement, and they belong where experiments belong. A voice with no `surfaces` key appears everywhere.
voices.title: TRANSLATOR — the reference in one ear and a second language in the other

layers.why: the other language, placed right and ANCHORED to the body at every phrase boundary

voices.note: THE VOICE THAT KEPT THE DELAY, ON PURPOSE. Everywhere else an overlay a beat behind the body is the bug — it is heard as a second person rather than as a timbre, which is why LEADER stopped being layered. Here it is the point: two speakers, placed apart, one following the other. `anchor` fits the second voice to the body at every phrase boundary rather than only at the sentence, so it tracks rather than wanders. CHOOSE THE LANGUAGE by changing the second layer's `voice` to any espeak-ng language code — fr, de, es, it, pt, ru, zh, ja, ko, hi, ar. HONEST LIMIT: espeak reads the TEXT IT IS GIVEN with that language's phonemes and prosody. It does not translate. Given English text a French voice produces English read by a French speaker, which is the interpreter-booth SOUND without the interpretation. Real translation needs a translation step feeding pre-translated text into the second layer, and the recipe already accepts that — it is a text source, not a language model.

voices.label: ZEN
voices._hidden: Reached only as ZEN's second face, never listed on its own.
voices.title: ZEN

layers.why: JAIMLA carries the words. The gender swap is a swap of the BODY — neural out, jaimla in — not a pitch shift on a male voice, because pitch is not gender.

the existing ZEN, placed opposite her and anchored at every phrase boundary. It is band-limited to 200-2400 Hz so it colours rather than competes — the same lesson LEADER cost: a layer with full-band energy is a second speaker.

voices.note: ZEN's second face: the same unhurried delivery in a female body, in stereo. The two are placed apart rather than summed, because depth comes from separation — that is the whole reason to have a second channel. A gentler version of LEADER's shaping: a small floor, the 420-640 Hz cut (mud reads as EFFORT, and effort is what this voice must never sound like), a clarity lift, and the top rolled off because sibilance reads as tension.

voices.label: vCLONE
voices.title: voice not cloned
voices.note: The hover says four words and stops there. An empty slot invites a question; a paragraph of roadmap answers a question nobody asked and dates badly. The clone tools are being built in mindX/voicey from ollywoo with faicey — when they land this entry gets an engine and a voice, and until then it says exactly what is true.

speeds._comment: playbackRate presets on the <audio> element. 0.666 is a requested preset. The slider is continuous over [min,max] and the presets are snap points on it.

templates._why: NEURAL IS A GOOD VOICE, SO IT IS WRITTEN DOWN. The `neural` entry is deliberately engine=auto with no voice, because that emits the exact query the reader sent before a picker existed and so keeps every cached NEURAL rendering valid. The cost of that is that NEURAL is defined by RESOLUTION, not by name: it is whatever pick('auto') returns and whatever piper calls its default. Install a second piper model that sorts first and NEURAL silently becomes a different voice. This template records what it actually resolved to, so the drift is detectable instead of invisible.

neural.verify: python -c "from utils.docspeech.engines import pick,Piper,voice_fingerprint; print(pick('auto').id, Piper().default_voice(), voice_fingerprint('piper',''))"
neural.note: If `verify` stops matching `fingerprint`, NEURAL has changed underneath the label. Either restore this model as piper's default, or set the `neural` entry's voice explicitly to en_GB-alan-medium — which pins it, at the cost of a new cache key for every NEURAL rendering.
